spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m0p5t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES cap, snap, dispensed
Init == cap = 2 /\ snap = 0 /\ dispensed = 0
Read == snap' = cap /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, dispensed>>
Reconfig == \E c \in {1, 2, 3} : cap' = c /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, dispensed>>
Commit == dispensed = 0 /\ snap # 0 /\ snap = cap /\ dispensed' = 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, snap>>
Retry == snap # cap /\ snap' = cap /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, dispensed>>
Next == Read \/ Reconfig \/ Commit \/ Retry
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<cap, snap, dispensed>>
DispenseAtMostOnce == dispensed <= 1
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DispenseAtMostOnce
nl:
A network of vending machines shares a single back-office ledger recording how many units of a promotional item remain. Each machine uses optimistic locking: before committing a sale it snapshots the current stock configuration, and it only finalizes the dispense if that snapshot still matches the live configuration at commit time. The operator can change a machine's shelf capacity at runtime, which bumps the live configuration and forces any in-flight sale to retry against the new value. A dispense physically drops a can and cannot be undone, so each authorized transaction must dispense exactly one unit and never twice. When a machine detects its snapshot is stale it simply re-reads and tries again rather than double-dropping. Modeled with the live capacity, a customer's snapshot, and a dispense counter.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the physical dispense action fires at most once per transaction, so the dispense counter never exceeds one.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m4p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES epoch, holder, queue
Init == epoch = 1 /\ holder = 0 /\ queue = 0
Rotate == epoch' = (epoch % 3) + 1 /\ holder' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED queue
Acquire == holder = 0 /\ holder' = epoch /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, queue>>
Release == holder # 0 /\ holder' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, queue>>
Enqueue == queue < 2 /\ queue' = queue + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder>>
Execute == queue > 0 /\ holder = epoch /\ queue' = queue - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, holder>>
Next == Rotate \/ Acquire \/ Release \/ Enqueue \/ Execute
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<epoch, holder, queue>>
NoStaleActor == holder = 0 \/ holder = epoch
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleActor
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network routes unlock commands through a small controller pool guarded by an authorization epoch. Commands wait in a bounded work queue; new commands are refused once the queue is full, which is the backpressure the hub uses to stay responsive. Only the controller currently holding authorization for the live epoch may dequeue and execute a command. When the operator rotates credentials the epoch advances and any controller that had grabbed authorization must drop it, because a controller running against a stale epoch is no longer authorized. A controller may be slow to release authorization but it does not crash, so the model tracks which epoch a holder presents. The concern is that a controller whose presented epoch no longer matches the live epoch must never be allowed to act.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a controller holds authorization, the epoch it presents equals the live authorization epoch, so no stale controller ever acts.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m6p3t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets
CONSTANT Slots, Labs
VARIABLES leases, reqs
Init == leases = {} /\ reqs = {}
Request == \E h \in Labs : h \notin reqs /\ reqs' = reqs \cup {h} /\ UNCHANGED leases
Grant ==
  \E h \in reqs, s \in Slots :
    (\A l \in leases : l.slot # s)
    /\ leases' = leases \cup {[slot |-> s, holder |-> h]}
    /\ reqs' = reqs \ {h}
Expire == \E l \in leases : leases' = leases \ {l} /\ UNCHANGED reqs
Next == Request \/ Grant \/ Expire
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<leases, reqs>>
NoDoubleAllocation == \A l1, l2 \in leases : (l1.slot = l2.slot) => (l1 = l2)
====
nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker hands out short-lived leases on cold-storage slots to requesting labs. A lab first files a request, and a granting service later assigns it a free slot by creating a lease record that names the slot and the holder. Because grant messages travel over an unreliable bus they can be delivered and applied in any order, so the granter must always re-check that the chosen slot has no live lease before creating one. Leases eventually expire and are removed, freeing the slot again. The critical requirement is that the same physical slot is never leased to two different labs at once, which would risk cross-contaminated units. State is a set of live lease records plus the set of pending requesters.
SAFETY PROPERTY: no two live leases ever name the same storage slot, so a slot is never double-allocated.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m4p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES book, opened
Init == book = 0 /\ opened = 0
Submit == book < 3 /\ book' = book + 1 /\ UNCHANGED opened
Cancel == book > 0 /\ book' = book - 1 /\ UNCHANGED opened
Open == opened = 0 /\ opened' = 1 /\ UNCHANGED book
Next == Submit \/ Cancel \/ Open
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<book, opened>>
OpenAtMostOnce == opened <= 1
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OpenAtMostOnce
nl:
A stock exchange runs an opening auction where orders accumulate before a single uncross event sets the opening price. Orders flow into a bounded book with backpressure: submissions are rejected once the book reaches its size limit. Cancellations can arrive and be applied in any order relative to submissions, so the book count moves up and down freely before the open. The uncross, or "opening print," is a physically irreversible market event that must happen at most once for the session; once the market has opened it cannot open a second time. The model tracks the resting order count and a one-shot opened flag. The safety concern is that the opening print never fires twice.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the irreversible opening-print event fires at most once, so the opened flag never exceeds one.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m4p4t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES queued, inflight
Init == queued = 0 /\ inflight = 0
Enqueue == queued < 3 /\ queued' = queued + 1 /\ UNCHANGED inflight
Take == queued > 0 /\ inflight < 2 /\ queued' = queued - 1 /\ inflight' = inflight + 1
Finish == inflight > 0 /\ inflight' = inflight - 1 /\ UNCHANGED queued
Next == Enqueue \/ Take \/ Finish
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<queued, inflight>>
WithinBounds == queued <= 3 /\ queued >= 0 /\ inflight <= 2 /\ inflight >= 0
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WithinBounds
nl:
A network of vending machines feeds restock jobs into a bounded work queue served by a small pool of restock workers. Enqueue is refused when the queue is full, providing backpressure so the dispatcher never overcommits. A worker takes a job off the queue into an in-flight processing set, and there is a hard limit on how many jobs may be in flight at once. Workers can be slow to finish a job but they do not fail, so an in-flight job may linger before it completes. The model tracks the queued count and the in-flight count. The safety concern is that neither the queue length nor the in-flight count ever exceeds its declared bound.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state the queued job count stays within the queue bound and the in-flight count stays within the worker bound.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od9m8p1t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Writers
VARIABLES coarse, fine, setpoint
Init == coarse = 0 /\ fine = 0 /\ setpoint = 0
AcquireCoarse == \E w \in Writers : coarse = 0 /\ coarse' = w /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, setpoint>>
AcquireFine == \E w \in Writers : coarse = w /\ fine = 0 /\ fine' = w /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, setpoint>>
Write == \E w \in Writers : fine = w /\ coarse = w /\ setpoint < 3 /\ setpoint' = setpoint + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine>>
ReleaseFine == fine # 0 /\ fine' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, setpoint>>
ReleaseCoarse == fine = 0 /\ coarse # 0 /\ coarse' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, setpoint>>
Next == AcquireCoarse \/ AcquireFine \/ Write \/ ReleaseFine \/ ReleaseCoarse
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarse, fine, setpoint>>
WritesSerialized == fine = 0 \/ fine = coarse
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Writers = {1, 2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT WritesSerialized
nl:
A power-grid load shedder guards a shared setpoint record with a two-level hierarchical lock: a coarse zone lock must be taken before the fine feeder lock. Two independent shedding instances share one pool of locks and both want to update the shared setpoint. The discipline is that a writer must hold the coarse lock and then the fine lock, with the same owner on both, before it may write; this serializes writers so their updates are never lost by an interleaving overwrite. Acquiring the fine lock requires already owning the coarse lock. A writer that owns both locks may bump the setpoint, then release both. The safety concern is that the fine lock is never held except by the same owner that holds the coarse lock, which is what prevents two instances from interleaving writes.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the fine feeder lock is held, it is held by the very owner that holds the coarse zone lock, so writers stay serialized.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m1p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES token, occupancy, cap
Init == token = 1 /\ occupancy = 0 /\ cap = 2
PassToken == token' = (token % 3) + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, cap>>
Dispatch == occupancy < cap /\ occupancy' = occupancy + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<token, cap>>
Complete == occupancy > 0 /\ occupancy' = occupancy - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<token, cap>>
Reconfig == \E c \in {2, 3} : c >= occupancy /\ cap' = c /\ UNCHANGED <<token, occupancy>>
Next == PassToken \/ Dispatch \/ Complete \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<token, occupancy, cap>>
CapacityRespected == occupancy >= 0 /\ occupancy <= cap
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT CapacityRespected
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper coordinates dispatch with a token ring: a single token circulates among the cars, and only the car currently holding the token may dispatch a run to the shared express floor. The express floor has a capacity limit on how many cars it can hold at once, and the building manager can reconfigure that capacity up or down at runtime, but never below the number of cars already there. The token is passed cyclically from one car to the next regardless of what else is happening. A dispatched car eventually completes its run and leaves the floor. The state tracks which car holds the token, how many cars occupy the floor, and the current capacity. The safety concern is that the number of cars on the express floor never exceeds the current capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: at all times the count of cars occupying the express floor is at most the current capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m9p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES ownerA, ownerB, epoch
Init == ownerA = 0 /\ ownerB = 0 /\ epoch = 0
ClaimA == ownerA = 0 /\ \E s \in {1, 2} : s # ownerB /\ ownerA' = s /\ UNCHANGED <<ownerB, epoch>>
ClaimB == ownerB = 0 /\ \E s \in {1, 2} : s # ownerA /\ ownerB' = s /\ UNCHANGED <<ownerA, epoch>>
ReleaseA == ownerA # 0 /\ ownerA' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<ownerB, epoch>>
ReleaseB == ownerB # 0 /\ ownerB' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<ownerA, epoch>>
Reconfig == epoch' = (epoch + 1) % 3 /\ ownerA' = 0 /\ ownerB' = 0
AdminOverride == \E s \in {1, 2} : ownerA' = s /\ ownerB' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED epoch
Next == ClaimA \/ ClaimB \/ ReleaseA \/ ReleaseB \/ Reconfig \/ AdminOverride
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<ownerA, ownerB, epoch>>
NoDoubleAssign == ownerA = 0 \/ ownerB = 0 \/ ownerA # ownerB
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleAssign
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network reconfigures itself with numbered epochs, and each reconfiguration assigns lock zones to controllers. Two controllers, A and B, may each claim a zone slot, and a slot number of zero means the controller holds nothing. A privileged admin can override the normal protocol to force-grant a zone to controller A while revoking B. Every reconfiguration advances the epoch and clears both controllers' claims so the new epoch starts clean. When a controller claims a zone it must pick a slot not currently held by the other controller. The safety concern is that the same zone slot is never held by both controllers at once, which would double-assign a physical lock.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the two controllers never simultaneously hold the same non-empty zone slot.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m3p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES leader, sessions, cap
Init == leader = 0 /\ sessions = 0 /\ cap = 3
Elect == leader = 0 /\ \E l \in {1, 2} : leader' = l /\ UNCHANGED <<sessions, cap>>
Failover == leader # 0 /\ leader' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<sessions, cap>>
OpenSession == leader # 0 /\ sessions < cap /\ sessions' = sessions + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, cap>>
CloseSession == sessions > 0 /\ sessions' = sessions - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, cap>>
AdminForce == \E l \in {1, 2} : leader' = l /\ UNCHANGED <<sessions, cap>>
Next == Elect \/ Failover \/ OpenSession \/ CloseSession \/ AdminForce
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<leader, sessions, cap>>
SessionsWithinCap == sessions >= 0 /\ sessions <= cap
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT SessionsWithinCap
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network elects a leader hub to coordinate unlock sessions, with automatic failover if the leader goes away. Only while a leader exists may new unlock sessions be opened, and there is a hard cap on how many sessions can be active at once. A privileged admin can force a specific hub to become leader, overriding the normal election. When the leader fails, the leader slot is cleared until a new one is elected. Sessions are opened one at a time up to the cap and closed as they finish. The state tracks the current leader, the active session count, and the cap. The safety concern is that the number of active unlock sessions never exceeds the cap.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the count of active unlock sessions is always at most the session cap.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od18m9p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES csA, csB, epoch
Init == csA = FALSE /\ csB = FALSE /\ epoch = 0
EnterA == csA = FALSE /\ csB = FALSE /\ csA' = TRUE /\ UNCHANGED <<csB, epoch>>
EnterB == csB = FALSE /\ csA = FALSE /\ csB' = TRUE /\ UNCHANGED <<csA, epoch>>
ExitA == csA = TRUE /\ csA' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED <<csB, epoch>>
ExitB == csB = TRUE /\ csB' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED <<csA, epoch>>
Reconfig == csA = FALSE /\ csB = FALSE /\ epoch' = (epoch + 1) % 3 /\ UNCHANGED <<csA, csB>>
Next == EnterA \/ EnterB \/ ExitA \/ ExitB \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<csA, csB, epoch>>
MutualExclusion == ~(csA /\ csB)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network uses epoch-numbered reconfiguration to manage a single master-lock critical section that two independent controller instances share from one pool. Each instance may enter the critical section to reprogram the master lock, but the protocol must guarantee they are never both inside at once. An instance enters only when the section is free and no other instance is inside, and it exits when done. Reconfiguration advances the epoch but may only run when neither instance is in the critical section. The state tracks whether instance A is inside, whether instance B is inside, and the current epoch. The safety concern is classic mutual exclusion: the two instances are never simultaneously in the critical section.
SAFETY PROPERTY: instances A and B are never both inside the master-lock critical section at the same time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od9m9p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES serving, shed, cap, epoch
Init == serving = 4 /\ shed = 0 /\ cap = 4 /\ epoch = 0
Shed == serving > 0 /\ serving' = serving - 1 /\ shed' = shed + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, epoch>>
Restore == shed > 0 /\ serving < cap /\ serving' = serving + 1 /\ shed' = shed - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, epoch>>
Reconfig == \E c \in {2, 3, 4} : c >= serving /\ cap' = c /\ epoch' = (epoch + 1) % 3 /\ UNCHANGED <<serving, shed>>
Next == Shed \/ Restore \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<serving, shed, cap, epoch>>
DemandConserved == serving + shed = 4 /\ serving >= 0 /\ shed >= 0
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT DemandConserved
nl:
A power-grid load shedder manages a fixed block of demand that is always either being served or deliberately shed; no demand is ever created or destroyed. Reconfiguration happens in numbered epochs, and the serving capacity can change at runtime as generation comes and goes. When the shedder sheds load it moves one unit from the served pile to the shed pile; when it restores load it moves a unit back, but only if serving stays within the current capacity. Each reconfiguration bumps the epoch and may adjust capacity. The state tracks the served amount, the shed amount, the current capacity, and the epoch. The safety concern is conservation: the served amount plus the shed amount always equals the fixed total demand.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the served amount plus the shed amount is invariant and always equals the fixed total demand.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m0p4t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES occupancy, cap, ver, snap
Init == occupancy = 0 /\ cap = 2 /\ ver = 0 /\ snap = 0
Read == snap' = ver /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, cap, ver>>
Admit == snap = ver /\ occupancy < cap /\ occupancy' = occupancy + 1 /\ ver' = (ver + 1) % 3 /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, snap>>
Depart == occupancy > 0 /\ occupancy' = occupancy - 1 /\ ver' = (ver + 1) % 3 /\ UNCHANGED <<cap, snap>>
Retry == snap # ver /\ snap' = ver /\ UNCHANGED <<occupancy, cap, ver>>
Next == Read \/ Admit \/ Depart \/ Retry
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<occupancy, cap, ver, snap>>
OccupancyWithinCap == occupancy >= 0 /\ occupancy <= cap
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT OccupancyWithinCap
nl:
A subway signalling block system controls how many trains occupy a shared track section, and two control centers share the same section from one pool. Each center uses optimistic locking: it snapshots a version stamp of the section, then admits a train only if its snapshot still matches the live version at commit time and the section is below capacity. Every admit or departure bumps the version stamp, so a center working from a stale snapshot will fail its check and must re-read. When a center's snapshot no longer matches the live version it simply refreshes and retries rather than admitting blindly. The state tracks the section occupancy, the capacity, the live version, and a center's snapshot. The safety concern is that occupancy never exceeds the section's capacity.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the number of trains occupying the shared section never exceeds the section capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od4m2p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES phase, voting, inBayA, inBayB, cap
Init == phase = "idle" /\ voting = 0 /\ inBayA = FALSE /\ inBayB = FALSE /\ cap = 2
Prepare == phase = "idle" /\ \E c \in {1, 2} : voting' = c /\ phase' = "prep" /\ UNCHANGED <<inBayA, inBayB, cap>>
CommitA == phase = "prep" /\ voting = 1 /\ inBayB = FALSE /\ inBayA' = TRUE /\ phase' = "idle" /\ voting' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<inBayB, cap>>
CommitB == phase = "prep" /\ voting = 2 /\ inBayA = FALSE /\ inBayB' = TRUE /\ phase' = "idle" /\ voting' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<inBayA, cap>>
Abort == phase = "prep" /\ phase' = "idle" /\ voting' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<inBayA, inBayB, cap>>
ExitA == inBayA = TRUE /\ inBayA' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, voting, inBayB, cap>>
ExitB == inBayB = TRUE /\ inBayB' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, voting, inBayA, cap>>
Reconfig == \E k \in {1, 2} : cap' = k /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, voting, inBayA, inBayB>>
Next == Prepare \/ CommitA \/ CommitB \/ Abort \/ ExitA \/ ExitB \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<phase, voting, inBayA, inBayB, cap>>
BayMutualExclusion == ~(inBayA /\ inBayB)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT BayMutualExclusion
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line admits cars to a single wash bay through a two-phase commit across the conveyor controller and the bay participant. In the prepare phase the controller nominates a car; the bay then either commits, moving that car into the bay, or aborts. The bay is a critical resource that only one car may occupy at a time, so a commit may only move a car in when the bay is free of the other car. Meanwhile the conveyor's buffer capacity can be reconfigured at runtime to model faster or slower feed rates. The state tracks the commit phase, which car (if any) occupies the bay via two occupancy flags, and the conveyor capacity. The safety concern is mutual exclusion of the wash bay: two cars are never in the bay at once.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the wash bay never holds two cars simultaneously.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m3p1t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES leader, doses, writeLock
Init == leader = 0 /\ doses = 0 /\ writeLock = 0
Elect == leader = 0 /\ \E l \in {1, 2} : leader' = l /\ UNCHANGED <<doses, writeLock>>
Failover == leader # 0 /\ leader' = 0 /\ writeLock' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED doses
BeginWrite == leader # 0 /\ writeLock = 0 /\ writeLock' = leader /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, doses>>
Commit == writeLock # 0 /\ writeLock = leader /\ doses' = (doses + 1) % 4 /\ writeLock' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED leader
Next == Elect \/ Failover \/ BeginWrite \/ Commit
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<leader, doses, writeLock>>
NoStaleWriter == writeLock = 0 \/ writeLock = leader
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleWriter
nl:
A pharmacy prescription dispenser keeps a shared count record of dispensed doses, updated only under a single elected leader with failover. Only the current leader may open a write session against the record, and while a write session is open it is stamped with the leader that owns it. A participant may be slow, leaving a write session open for a while before it commits the increment, but it does not crash arbitrarily. If the leader fails over, the leader slot is cleared and any in-flight write session must be cleared with it, so no stale session lingers past the leadership change. The state tracks the current leader, the dose count, and which leader owns the open write session. The safety concern is that any open write session is owned by the current leader, which is what prevents lost updates from a stale writer.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a write session is open, it is owned by the current leader, so no stale session can overwrite the record.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od2m6p3t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES bin1, bin2, ttl1, ttl2
Init == bin1 = 0 /\ bin2 = 0 /\ ttl1 = 0 /\ ttl2 = 0
Acquire1 == bin1 = 0 /\ \E b \in {1, 2} : b # bin2 /\ bin1' = b /\ ttl1' = 2 /\ UNCHANGED <<bin2, ttl2>>
Acquire2 == bin2 = 0 /\ \E b \in {1, 2} : b # bin1 /\ bin2' = b /\ ttl2' = 2 /\ UNCHANGED <<bin1, ttl1>>
Decay1 == bin1 # 0 /\ ttl1 > 0 /\ ttl1' = ttl1 - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<bin1, bin2, ttl2>>
Decay2 == bin2 # 0 /\ ttl2 > 0 /\ ttl2' = ttl2 - 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<bin1, bin2, ttl1>>
Expire1 == bin1 # 0 /\ ttl1 = 0 /\ bin1' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<bin2, ttl1, ttl2>>
Expire2 == bin2 # 0 /\ ttl2 = 0 /\ bin2' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<bin1, ttl1, ttl2>>
Next == Acquire1 \/ Acquire2 \/ Decay1 \/ Decay2 \/ Expire1 \/ Expire2
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<bin1, bin2, ttl1, ttl2>>
NoSharedBin == bin1 = 0 \/ bin2 = 0 \/ bin1 # bin2
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoSharedBin
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet leases storage bins, and two robots draw from one shared pool of bins under lease-based ownership with expiry. Each robot may hold at most one bin at a time, indicated by a bin number with zero meaning it holds none. When a robot acquires a bin it must pick one the other robot is not currently holding, and it starts a lease timer. The lease counts down over time and, once it reaches zero, the bin is released back to the pool. A robot may re-lease only a free bin. The state tracks each robot's held bin and each robot's remaining lease time. The safety concern is that the two robots never hold the same bin at the same time, which would double-allocate a physical slot.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the two robots never simultaneously hold the same non-empty bin.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od5m3p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES host, hostTerm, term, cap
Init == host = 0 /\ hostTerm = 0 /\ term = 1 /\ cap = 2
Elect == host = 0 /\ \E h \in {1, 2} : host' = h /\ hostTerm' = term /\ UNCHANGED <<term, cap>>
Failover == host # 0 /\ host' = 0 /\ hostTerm' = 0 /\ term' = (term % 3) + 1 /\ UNCHANGED cap
Match == host # 0 /\ hostTerm = term /\ UNCHANGED <<host, hostTerm, term, cap>>
Reconfig == \E k \in {2, 3} : cap' = k /\ UNCHANGED <<host, hostTerm, term>>
Next == Elect \/ Failover \/ Match \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<host, hostTerm, term, cap>>
FreshHostOnly == host = 0 \/ hostTerm = term
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FreshHostOnly
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker elects a host to run each lobby, with failover if the host drops. The host is stamped with the election term under which it won, and the live term advances on every failover. Only a host whose stamped term equals the live term is fresh enough to admit players; a host carrying a stale term must not act. The lobby capacity can be reconfigured at runtime as server load changes. When the host fails over, the host slot is cleared and the term advances, so any later-arriving stale host is rejected. The state tracks the current host, the term stamped on that host, the live term, and the lobby capacity. The safety concern is that no host with a stale term ever performs matchmaking.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a host is present, the term stamped on it equals the live term, so no stale host acts.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od0m2p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES phase, writer, bookings
Init == phase = "idle" /\ writer = 0 /\ bookings = 0
Prepare == phase = "idle" /\ \E w \in {1, 2} : writer' = w /\ phase' = "prepared" /\ UNCHANGED bookings
Commit == phase = "prepared" /\ writer # 0 /\ bookings' = (bookings + 1) % 4 /\ phase' = "idle" /\ writer' = 0
Abort == phase = "prepared" /\ phase' = "idle" /\ writer' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED bookings
AdminOverride == phase = "prepared" /\ phase' = "idle" /\ writer' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED bookings
Next == Prepare \/ Commit \/ Abort \/ AdminOverride
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<phase, writer, bookings>>
PreparedHasWriter == (phase = "prepared") => (writer # 0)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT PreparedHasWriter
nl:
A hospital operating-room scheduler updates a shared bookings record through a two-phase commit across the scheduling participants. In the prepare phase one participant is nominated as the writer for the pending transaction; the commit phase then applies exactly that writer's update to the bookings record, and an abort discards it. A privileged admin can override an in-flight transaction, safely cancelling it and returning the coordinator to idle. The discipline that prevents lost updates is that whenever a transaction is prepared, it has a definite non-zero writer that owns the pending update; the record is never mutated by a phantom writer. The state tracks the commit phase, the nominated writer, and the bookings count. The safety concern is that a prepared transaction always has a valid owning writer.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the coordinator is in the prepared phase, the pending transaction has a non-zero owning writer.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m3p6t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES lead, term, cmdTerm
Init == lead = 0 /\ term = 1 /\ cmdTerm = 0
Elect == lead = 0 /\ \E l \in {1, 2} : lead' = l /\ UNCHANGED <<term, cmdTerm>>
Latch == lead # 0 /\ cmdTerm = 0 /\ cmdTerm' = term /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, term>>
Execute == cmdTerm # 0 /\ cmdTerm' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<lead, term>>
Failover == lead # 0 /\ lead' = 0 /\ term' = (term % 3) + 1 /\ cmdTerm' = 0
Next == Elect \/ Latch \/ Execute \/ Failover
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<lead, term, cmdTerm>>
NoStaleCommand == cmdTerm = 0 \/ cmdTerm = term
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleCommand
nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm elects a lead drone to issue survey commands, with failover if the lead is lost. The live command term advances every time leadership fails over. A command issued by the lead is latched and stamped with the term current at issue time; the latched command may take a while to execute because a drone can be slow, but it does not fail outright. If leadership fails over while a command is still latched, that in-flight command must be invalidated along with the term change, so a command stamped with an old term is never left executing. The state tracks the current lead drone, the live term, and the term stamped on any latched command. The safety concern is that a latched command's stamped term always matches the live term, so no stale command runs.
SAFETY PROPERTY: any latched survey command carries the live term, so a stale-term command never remains in force.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m4p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES queue, epoch, dispEpoch
Init == queue = 0 /\ epoch = 1 /\ dispEpoch = 0
Enqueue == queue < 2 /\ queue' = queue + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, dispEpoch>>
Dispatch == queue > 0 /\ dispEpoch = 0 /\ dispEpoch' = epoch /\ queue' = queue - 1 /\ UNCHANGED epoch
Complete == dispEpoch # 0 /\ dispEpoch' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, epoch>>
Reconfig == epoch' = (epoch % 3) + 1 /\ dispEpoch' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED queue
AdminOverride == queue' = 0 /\ dispEpoch' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED epoch
Next == Enqueue \/ Dispatch \/ Complete \/ Reconfig \/ AdminOverride
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<queue, epoch, dispEpoch>>
NoStaleDispatch == dispEpoch = 0 \/ dispEpoch = epoch
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoStaleDispatch
nl:
An elevator bank routes floor-call requests through a bounded work queue with backpressure: new calls are refused once the queue is full. Dispatch is governed by an authorization epoch, and a dispatched call is latched with the epoch that was live when it was picked. A privileged admin override can clear the whole system at once. When the operator reconfigures the bank the epoch advances and any latched in-flight dispatch must be invalidated, because a dispatch stamped with a superseded epoch is no longer authorized. The state tracks the queued call count, the live epoch, and the epoch stamped on any latched dispatch. The safety concern is that a latched dispatch always carries the live epoch, so no stale or unauthorized dispatch executes.
SAFETY PROPERTY: any latched dispatch carries the live epoch, so no dispatch stamped with a stale epoch remains in force.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od8m8p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Workers
VARIABLES coarse, fine, enrolled, cap
Init == coarse = 0 /\ fine = 0 /\ enrolled = 0 /\ cap = 2
AcquireCoarse == \E w \in Workers : coarse = 0 /\ coarse' = w /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, enrolled, cap>>
AcquireFine == \E w \in Workers : coarse = w /\ fine = 0 /\ fine' = w /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, enrolled, cap>>
Enroll == \E w \in Workers : fine = w /\ coarse = w /\ enrolled < cap /\ enrolled' = enrolled + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, cap>>
ReleaseFine == fine # 0 /\ fine' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, enrolled, cap>>
ReleaseCoarse == fine = 0 /\ coarse # 0 /\ coarse' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, enrolled, cap>>
Reconfig == \E k \in {2, 3} : k >= enrolled /\ cap' = k /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, fine, enrolled>>
Next == AcquireCoarse \/ AcquireFine \/ Enroll \/ ReleaseFine \/ ReleaseCoarse \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<coarse, fine, enrolled, cap>>
FineImpliesCoarse == fine = 0 \/ fine = coarse
====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Workers = {1, 2}
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT FineImpliesCoarse
nl:
A university course-registration system protects a shared enrollment record with hierarchical locks: a coarse department lock must be taken before a fine section lock, and only a holder of both may record an enrollment. Two registration workers contend for the locks. Acquiring the fine lock requires already owning the coarse lock, and enrollments are recorded one seat at a time up to the current section capacity, which the registrar can change at runtime as rooms are reassigned. This lock hierarchy serializes writers so concurrent updates to the enrollment record are never lost. The state tracks the coarse-lock owner, the fine-lock owner, the enrolled count, and the capacity. The safety concern is that the fine lock is never held except by the same worker that holds the coarse lock.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever the fine section lock is held, it is held by the same worker that holds the coarse department lock.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od17m7p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES reg, snap, committed, ceil
Init == reg = 0 /\ snap = 0 /\ committed = 0 /\ ceil = 3
Read == snap' = reg /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, committed, ceil>>
Swap == snap = reg /\ reg < ceil /\ reg' = reg + 1 /\ committed' = committed + 1 /\ snap' = reg + 1 /\ UNCHANGED ceil
Retry == snap # reg /\ snap' = reg /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, committed, ceil>>
Reconfig == \E k \in {3, 4} : k >= reg /\ ceil' = k /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, snap, committed>>
Next == Read \/ Swap \/ Retry \/ Reconfig
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<reg, snap, committed, ceil>>
NoLostUpdate == reg = committed
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoLostUpdate
nl:
An airport baggage router updates a shared routing register with a compare-and-swap primitive. A worker snapshots the register, then attempts a swap that succeeds only if the register still equals the snapshot, at which point it advances the register by one and records one committed update; if the snapshot is stale the worker re-reads and tries again rather than writing blindly. Because every committed swap advances the register by exactly one and bumps the committed-update counter by exactly one, the register and the committed count move in lockstep and no update is ever lost. The register ceiling is a runtime capacity the operator can raise or lower. The state tracks the register, the pending snapshot, the committed-update count, and the ceiling. The safety concern is that the register value always equals the number of committed updates.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the routing register always equals the count of committed updates, so no compare-and-swap update is ever lost.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od1m4p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES usingA, usingB, queue
Init == usingA = FALSE /\ usingB = FALSE /\ queue = 0
Enqueue == queue < 2 /\ queue' = queue + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<usingA, usingB>>
SeizeA == usingA = FALSE /\ usingB = FALSE /\ queue > 0 /\ usingA' = TRUE /\ queue' = queue - 1 /\ UNCHANGED usingB
SeizeB == usingB = FALSE /\ usingA = FALSE /\ queue > 0 /\ usingB' = TRUE /\ queue' = queue - 1 /\ UNCHANGED usingA
ReleaseA == usingA = TRUE /\ usingA' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED <<usingB, queue>>
ReleaseB == usingB = TRUE /\ usingB' = FALSE /\ UNCHANGED <<usingA, queue>>
Next == Enqueue \/ SeizeA \/ SeizeB \/ ReleaseA \/ ReleaseB
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<usingA, usingB, queue>>
RunwayExclusive == ~(usingA /\ usingB)
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT RunwayExclusive
nl:
An air-traffic runway allocator serializes access to a single runway that two control instances share from one pool. Landing requests accumulate in a bounded queue with backpressure, refused once the queue is full. To land a flight, a control instance seizes the runway, which it may do only when the runway is free of the other instance, and doing so consumes one queued request. When the landing completes the instance releases the runway. The runway is a critical resource, so the two instances must never both hold it at once. The state tracks whether instance A holds the runway, whether instance B holds it, and the queued-request count. The safety concern is mutual exclusion: the runway is never held by both control instances simultaneously.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the runway is never held by both control instances at the same time.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m0p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES blk1, blk2, crashed1
Init == blk1 = 0 /\ blk2 = 0 /\ crashed1 = FALSE
Claim1 == crashed1 = FALSE /\ blk1 = 0 /\ \E b \in {1, 2} : b # blk2 /\ blk1' = b /\ UNCHANGED <<blk2, crashed1>>
Release1 == blk1 # 0 /\ blk1' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<blk2, crashed1>>
Crash1 == crashed1 = FALSE /\ crashed1' = TRUE /\ UNCHANGED <<blk1, blk2>>
Claim2 == blk2 = 0 /\ \E b \in {1, 2} : b # blk1 /\ blk2' = b /\ UNCHANGED <<blk1, crashed1>>
Release2 == blk2 # 0 /\ blk2' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<blk1, crashed1>>
Next == Claim1 \/ Release1 \/ Crash1 \/ Claim2 \/ Release2
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_<<blk1, blk2, crashed1>>
NoCollision == blk1 = 0 \/ blk2 = 0 \/ blk1 # blk2
====
cfg_text:
INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoCollision
nl:
A subway signalling block system lets two trains contend for track blocks under optimistic locking, where a train claims a free block only after checking the other train is not on it. Each train holds at most one block, with zero meaning none. Train one can crash silently: at any point it may simply stop taking further actions, but any block it already holds remains held until explicitly released, and it stops issuing new claims. Train two keeps operating normally. A claim is permitted only for a block the other train does not currently occupy. The state tracks each train's occupied block and whether train one has crashed. The safety concern is that the two trains never occupy the same block at once, which would be a signalling collision.
SAFETY PROPERTY: the two trains never occupy the same non-empty block simultaneously.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od4m5p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
VARIABLES votes, cars1, cars2, crashed
Init == votes = 0 /\ cars1 = 0 /\ cars2 = 0 /\ crashed = FALSE
Vote == votes < 2 /\ votes' = votes + 1 /\ UNCHANGED <<cars1, cars2, crashed>>
AdmitBay1 == votes >= 2 /\ cars1 = 0 /\ cars1' = 1 /\ votes' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<cars2, crashed>>
AdmitBay2 == votes >= 2 /\ cars2 = 0 /\ cars2' = 1 /\ votes' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<cars1, crashed>>
Finish1 == cars1 > 0 /\ cars1' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, cars2, crashed>>
Finish2 == cars2 > 0 /\ cars2' = 0 /\ UNCHANGED <<votes, cars1, crashed>>

====
cfg_text:

NEXT Next
INVARIANT NoDoubleOccupancy
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line decides admissions by quorum voting: a shared set of voters must reach a quorum before a car is admitted to one of two wash bays. Votes accumulate toward the quorum; once quorum is reached, one car is admitted into a chosen bay and the vote tally resets. Each bay holds at most one car, tracked as a per-bay car count. One voter may crash silently and simply stop participating, which the model marks with a crash flag but which does not prevent the remaining voters from forming quorum. A finished car leaves its bay. The state tracks the vote tally, the car count in each bay, and the crash flag. The safety concern is that no bay is ever double-allocated, that is, no bay ever holds more than one car.
SAFETY PROPERTY: each wash bay holds at most one car at any time, so a bay slot is never double-allocated.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m8p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals
CONSTANT Instances
VARIABLES coarse, fine, inBlock
Init == coarse = 0 /\ fine = 0 /\ inBlock = 0
AcquireCoarse == \E w \in Instances : coarse = 0 /\ coarse' = w /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, inBlock>>
AcquireFine == \E w \in Instances : coarse = w /\ fine = 0 /\ fine' = w /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, inBlock>>

cfg_text:
CONSTANTS Instances = {1, 2}

NEXT Next
INVARIANT BlockHeldUnderLocks
nl:
A subway signalling block system guards a single critical block with hierarchical locks that two independent control instances share from one pool: a coarse route lock must be taken before a fine block lock, and only a holder of both may enter the block. To enter the critical block, an instance must own both the coarse and fine locks under its own name; on exit it leaves the block and drops both locks. Acquiring the fine lock requires already holding the coarse lock. The state tracks the coarse-lock owner, the fine-lock owner, and which instance, if any, currently occupies the block. The safety concern, a form of mutual exclusion enforced by the lock hierarchy, is that whoever occupies the block holds both the coarse and fine locks.
SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever an instance occupies the critical block, it holds both the coarse route lock and the fine block lock.
